title: A-2000 assembly & design review
registerRevision: 2026-09-10 · Physical equipment ownership and complete Explore assemblies
lead: Water recovery: RO feed equalization T-2001 with feed / backwash pump P-2001, pretreatment MMF-2001 → GF-2001 → CF-2001 → UF-2001, high-pressure pumps P-2002 and single-pass RO-2001 (modelled as three trains A / B duty, C standby), permeate storage T-2002 with distribution pump P-2005 and polishing CF-2002, concentrate storage T-2003 / P-2003, antiscalant T-2004 / P-2004, CIP skid CIP-2001 and the model-side UF, backwash and spent-CIP buffers, tie-in station BL-A2000 and control station CP-2000.

findings.status: No basis approved — follows the A-1000 case
findings.reason: An RO plant is sized on its feed flow and quality and on the permeate demand; neither is fixed until the A-1000 discharge route and acid-recovery case are decided.
findings.observation: D-A2000-01 withdraws the RO-2001 feed basis and approves only the design statement that A-2000 sizing follows the acid-recovery decision (REP-039) and the A-1000 discharge route: the process-water demand build-up gives 8–18 m³/h net permeate (REP-008) against 17–120 m³/h of A-1000 effluent by case (REP-038). PFD-2000 has no stream table. The model's T-2001 1,000 m³, T-2002 140 m³ and T-2003 95 m³ are screening allowances, and the three RO trains A / B / C with P-2002 A / B / C exist only in the model — LST-001 and PFD-2000 list one RO-2001 and one P-2002.
findings.action: Decide the A-1000 case, then issue the first A-2000 stream table on DBM V2.0 with the recovery, permeate quality and concentrate route; reconcile the three-train configuration with LST-001 / PFD-2000.

findings.topic: RO feed condition — oxidiser, scaling and the NaOH question
findings.reason: The RO membrane tolerates neither residual oxidiser nor a feed beyond its sulphate scaling limit; the upstream chemistry decides whether RO is workable at all.
findings.observation: D-A2000-02 approves REP-038 as the process constraint: RO feed must be oxidiser-free and within BaSO₄ / CaSO₄ scaling limits; lime-stage gypsum saturation (≈ 1,480 mg/L) governs recovery; no NaOH upstream, because Na₂SO₄ at 61 g/L makes RO unworkable — which ties this area to the A-1000 flowsheet decision. P-2002 is approved as a 12–16 bar high-pressure pump (MAT-002 service register) as a screening basis. The model provides carbon filtration CF-2001 for oxidant / organic reduction and antiscalant dosing T-2004 / P-2004 ahead of the trains.
findings.action: Carry the oxidiser-free and scaling constraints into the A-1000 MoC (lime-first, no NaOH) and into the RO design basis; confirm the antiscalant and recovery against the gypsum limit once the feed is fixed.

findings.reason: The activated-carbon filter CF-2001 is the only pretreatment left (D-A2000-03: clean condensate); its backwash is taken from the permeate tank T-2002 and returns to A-1000 T-1006, and must be sized with it.
findings.observation: The multimedia, greensand and ultrafiltration pretreatment (MMF-2001, GF-2001, UF-2001) and its buffer tank, pumps and backwash collection were retired by D-A2000-03 and removed from the model. CF-2001 filters the T-2001 condensate and is backwashed with RO permeate from T-2002 through P-2005; the backwash waste joins the RO reject to A-1000 T-1006. The control station CP-2000 remains model-only and is not on LST-001; no filtration duty is approved.
findings.action: Size CF-2001 and its permeate backwash on the A-2000 stream table; register CP-2000 or record it by decision; state the backwash return in the A-1000 balance.

findings.reason: Sequential acid / alkaline cleaning liquor is a segregated waste and must not reach the RO feed or the A-1000 lime stage uncontrolled.
findings.observation: The model provides the register CIP skid CIP-2001 with recirculation pump P-CIP2001, a segregated spent-CIP hold TK-CIP2001-W (5 m³ allowance) with transfer pump P-CIP2001-W, and the antiscalant day tank T-2004 / P-2004. The CIP chemistry, frequency and spent-liquor destination are not defined; the spent-CIP tank and the two CIP pumps (P-CIP2001, P-CIP2001-W) exist only as model geometry without semantic records.
findings.action: Define the CIP chemistry and cycle with the membrane selection; assign the spent-CIP destination (A-1000 stage or off-site); register the model-only tags.

findings.reason: Pretreated, low-solids water at up to 16 bar sets pressure-vessel and pump materials; the membranes themselves are a selection, not a material ruling.
findings.observation: D-A2000-MOC applies MAT-002 to fourteen items with the RO service row — TFC polyamide RO elements in FRP pressure vessels, with the matching tank, pump, filter-housing and CIP selections; MDL-001 (HDPE / XLPE tanks, 316L pumps and housings, PVDF UF modules) superseded. The single MAT-002 row covers the whole area, so the tank and pump wording is generic and will need item-level refinement at datasheet stage.
findings.action: Refine MAT-002 per item (tanks, pumps, filter housings, UF modules) once the stream table exists; keep the TFC / FRP RO selection.

findings.topic: A-2000 on clean sources only (D-A2000-03): condensate polishing and municipal make-up; the A-1000 effluent is not reclaimed; 15 tags retired
findings.status: Basis approved; datasheets issued as candidates; demand held on A-400 (H-01)
findings.reason: D-A2000-01 left A-2000 unsized until the acid route and the A-1000 discharge were settled (A2000-01); with Route 2 + 6 both are now known, and the effluent turned out to be the wrong source.
findings.observation: On the Case 4 volumes the A-300 phase 2 HCl dominates the A-1000 effluent: ≈ 5.9 g/L chloride and ≈ 12 g/L TDS at the M3 estimate, ≈ 29 g/L chloride and ≈ 48 g/L TDS at the PFD dose — lime does not remove chloride. Reclaiming it would need brackish-to-seawater RO and 4–26 t/d of soda-ash softening, against ≈ 380 m³/d of municipal water (≈ $0.15–0.3 M/y). D-A2000-03 on bases A2-1–A2-8 approved by QFL 2026-09-27 (FEED-PE-CAL-036, FEED-PE-DAT-132…139, register V9.0) puts A-2000 on clean sources only: the A-1100 condensate (2.6 m³/h, 3.0 at the 150 t/d rating) is pH-trimmed in T-2001 (re-purposed, 15 m³), passed through carbon (CF-2001) and polished on RO-2001A/B (1 + 1, 85 %, 10 bar, P-2002A/B) to ≈ 2.2 m³/h; ≈ 15.8 m³/h of municipal water enters through CF-2002 (IF-A2000-CITY); T-2002 (100 m³, 4 h) and P-2005A/B (20 m³/h × 35 m) serve the 18 m³/h demand. The RO reject (≈ 0.5 m³/h) goes to T-1006 and the A-1000 effluent to sewer. The media / greensand / UF train, the backwash and brine handling and the third RO train — 15 tags — are retired; the CAL-036 feed basis, design concept and 10 bar feed pressure replace the D-A2000-01 / -02 statements; 12 missing-value gaps close. W1 (reclaim) stays a noted option, gated on M3 and a water-reuse requirement.
findings.action: Settle the A-400 demand (hold H-01) and scale T-2002 / P-2005 / the municipal allowance to it; obtain the municipal supply data (pressure, hardness, connection); confirm the condensate quality with the concentrator vendor (M5) and on reconcentrated M1 filtrate (M2); raise the PFD-2000 MoC and LST-001 entries; remove the retired tags from the model.

findings.topic: Model catch-up release 1 (D-MDL-01): the W3 retirements shown in place; T-2001 / T-2002 at datasheet volumes
findings.status: Model updated — retired equipment removed and W3 routes drawn (V280)
findings.reason: The model drew the PFD-2000 reclaim plant that D-A2000-03 retired; V280 removes it.
findings.observation: MMF-2001, GF-2001, UF-2001, P-2001, TK-UF2001, P-UF2001, TK-BW2001, P-BW2001, T-2003, P-2003 and the third RO train (GF-RO2001C, P-2002C, RO-2001C) are removed from the model with their streams (D-A2000-03, V280). T-2001 is the 15 m³ condensate receiver (FEED-PE-DAT-132) fed from the blinded A-1100 condensate boundary and T-2002 is 100 m³ (FEED-PE-DAT-136); RO reject, relief and the carbon-filter backwash return to A-1000 T-1006, and CF-2002 feeds city make-up into T-2002.
findings.action: Carry the compact re-layout of the remaining equipment (stage 2) and confirm the A-1100 condensate tie-in under Route 2 + 6.

findings.topic: Model catch-up release 2: W3 re-labels and the IF-A2000-CITY battery limit
findings.status: Model labels updated — routes with the model engineer
findings.reason: CF-2001, CF-2002 and T-2004 / P-2004 were re-purposed by D-A2000-03 and IF-A2000-CITY had no model marker.
findings.observation: CF-2001 is labelled as the condensate carbon filter (FEED-PE-DAT-133), CF-2002 as the municipal make-up cartridge filter (FEED-PE-DAT-138) and T-2004 / P-2004 as the RO dosing skid (FEED-PE-DAT-139); an IF-A2000-CITY battery-limit marker stands at the east block edge beside CF-2002. The municipal line itself is not routed.
findings.action: Route the municipal make-up to CF-2002 and T-2002 with the W3 re-routing (model engineer); obtain the municipal supply data.

findings.topic: Stale-text clean-up (D-A2000-04): T-2001 / CF-2001 register and study text superseded
findings.status: Superseded — datasheets govern; LST-001 revision to raise
findings.reason: The explorer still showed T-2001 as the RO feed equalization tank and CF-2001 as filtering ahead of ultrafiltration.
findings.observation: D-A2000-04 (stale-text clean-up B1, approved by QFL 2026-09-29): the LST-001 name and the MDL-001 43.5 m³/h equalization basis of T-2001 are superseded by FEED-PE-DAT-132 (15 m³ condensate receiver), and the LST-001 function of CF-2001 by FEED-PE-DAT-133 (condensate carbon filter). DAT-132 / DAT-136 are read at their register V11.8 revisions (Sheet 2 added).
findings.action: Raise the FEED-PE-LST-001 revision for T-2001 / CF-2001 (register owner).

findings.topic: Retired pretreatment tags marked; P-2002 / P-2005 lettered (LST-001 V5.2)
findings.reason: LST-001 V5.2 tag-allocation catch-up (register V12.5, bases T1–T9, QFL 2026-09-29).
findings.observation: FEED-PE-LST-001 V5.2 (register V12.5; bases T1–T9 approved in review by QFL 2026-09-29) catches the register up with the issued datasheets: 42 new tags (status “New V5.2” — not on PFD V5.1.1, connections as text, PFD MoC pending, FLG-016), duty / standby units lettered per datasheet, 16 retired tags kept and marked, C-301 / P-303 re-typed. The data layer reads the archived V5.1 first (existing valueIds unchanged) and appends V5.2 last; V5.2 supersedes the V5.1 register name / function rows in full and replaces the V5.1 stream rows; identity.esrStatus records New / Retired. A-2000: MMF-2001, GF-2001, UF-2001, P-2001, T-2003 and P-2003 are marked retired (D-A2000-03); P-2002 and P-2005 are lettered A/B per DAT-135 / DAT-137, so twelve lettered-unit pump gaps close on the group datasheet rows. The model third RO train and the backwash / UF / CIP sub-package tags stay model-only (GAP-A-2000-ID-d8f929, GAP-A-2000-ID-d0aead).
findings.action: Raise the PFD-001 MoC (LST-001 FLG-016) to draw the new items and number their streams.

decisions.rationale: Plant-wide ruling: FEED-PE-MAT-002 'Recommended MOC (base case)' governs material of construction over FEED-PE-MDL-001 (scale-up study) and design-note wording — MAT-002 is the controlled MoC matrix and postdates MDL-001. Wording variants of the same material family are superseded by the MAT-002 statement.
8–18 m³/h net permeate (REP-008, demand build-up) vs 17–120 m³/h A-1000 effluent by case (REP-038): feed and product bases not reconciled; PFD-2000 has no stream table.
decisions.gapNote: Decide the A-1000 discharge route and the spent-acid recovery case (REP-039: 150–200 t/d reconcentration; MOC-001 Part D.1) before any A-1000 / A-2000 sizing; then issue the first A-1000 / A-2000 stream tables (none exist) on DBM V2.0 with the wastewater range by case (REP-038).

decisions.rationale: A-2000 sizing follows the acid-recovery decision and the A-1000 discharge route — do not freeze.

RO feed must be oxidiser-free and within BaSO₄ / CaSO₄ scaling limits; gypsum saturation ≈ 1,480 mg/L governs recovery; no NaOH upstream (Na₂SO₄ 61 g/L makes RO unworkable) — adopted as the process constraint.
12–16 bar high-pressure pump (MAT-002 M-061 service register) — screening basis.
decisions.gapNote: Reconcile the model's three RO trains (RO-2001A/B/C, P-2002A/B/C) and the backwash / UF / CIP sub-package tags with LST-001 / PFD-2000 once the A-2000 stream table exists.

decisions.rationale: A-2000 on clean sources only (W3, bases A2-1–A2-8, FEED-PE-CAL-036): on the Case 4 volumes the A-300 phase 2 HCl leaves ≈ 5.9–29 g/L chloride (≈ 12–48 g/L TDS) in the A-1000 effluent, so reclaiming it would need brackish-to-seawater RO and 4–26 t/d of soda-ash softening against ≈ 380 m³/d of municipal water. A-2000 polishes the A-1100 condensate (carbon + 1 + 1 RO, ≈ 2.2 m³/h) and takes ≈ 15.8 m³/h of municipal make-up for the 18 m³/h demand; the A-1000 effluent goes to sewer. Approved in review by QFL 2026-09-27.
decisions.gapNote: Final demand (A-400 hold H-01); condensate quality (M2 / M5); municipal supply data (IF-A2000-CITY); PFD-2000 MoC and LST-001; remove the retired tags from the model; W1 only if M3 cuts the HCl and reuse becomes a requirement

decisions.rationale: Supersedes the D-A2000-01 statement: A-2000 no longer follows the A-1000 discharge — it treats clean sources only.
10 bar on low-TDS condensate replaces the 12–16 bar screening basis of D-A2000-02.
LST-001 V5.1 lists T-2001 as the RO feed equalization tank; superseded by FEED-PE-DAT-132 (15 m³ condensate receiver, D-A2000-03). Stale-text clean-up B1, approved by QFL 2026-09-29.
The MDL-001 RO-feed equalization basis (43.5 m³/h) is superseded by FEED-PE-DAT-132 (D-A2000-03). Stale-text clean-up B1, approved by QFL 2026-09-29.
LST-001 V5.1 function names ultrafiltration (retired); superseded by FEED-PE-DAT-133 (condensate carbon filter). Stale-text clean-up B1, approved by QFL 2026-09-29.
